source_spans.quote:
(a) 
            Application.
             An employer must have an emergency action plan whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one. The requirements in this section apply to each such emergency action plan.

claim_judgments.rationale: C0000 states an unconditional requirement that an employer must have an emergency action plan, omitting the critical statutory condition 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one' as well as the application clause in 1910.38(a). This renders the scope impermissibly overbroad and the summary inaccurate.

source_spans.quote:
(a) 
            Application.
             An employer must have an emergency action plan whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one. The requirements in this section apply to each such emergency action plan.

(b) 
            Written and oral emergency action plans.
             An emergency action plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available to employees for review. However, an employer with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally to employees.

claim_judgments.rationale: C0001 captures the general rule that an emergency action plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available for employee review, but fails to incorporate or reference the exception in paragraph (b) for employers with 10 or fewer employees who may communicate the plan orally. This causes the stated scope and summary to be overbroad relative to the source rule.

             An emergency action plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available to employees for review. However, an employer with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally to employees.

claim_judgments.rationale: C0002 accurately extracts the permissive exception in 1910.38(b), allowing employers with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally to employees rather than maintaining a written plan.
